report:
Stage comparison uses the first 19 focal records as the initial set and P08–P13 plus R01 as additions, as indicated by the supplied ordering; no separate initial-stage artifact was supplied.

Initial stage: Packaging reception is favorable but qualified. P00’s metal-packaging praise has 296 displayed likes, supporting resonance with that statement, not verified environmental performance. P03 is the same actor elaborating with tentative recyclability/reuse claims; P01 is brand agreement, not independent confirmation. P02 questions recyclability. Distinct accounts praise appearance and packaging care, while P26 asks what the product actually does for skin. P15’s planned empty-container reuse has 150 likes but is not completed reuse or evidence of suitability for medication storage. Refill-bundle requests, sticker confusion and P42’s discovery of refillability after receipt expose specific interests and information gaps. Exact packaging SKU/version remains unknown: Continuum is explicitly named in P17’s shipment and P27’s bundle request, but those references cannot identify every commenter’s product.

Initially, P06 alone reports an arrival leak with a loose top, cleanup and concern about oxygen exposure (12 likes). The narrow arrival-failure proposition is initially isolated as firsthand testimony; engagement is visible, but exposure context is insufficient to confidently award material resonance. P07 offers a replacement and says short exposure is not an issue: these are brand service/advice statements, not independently verified product safety or a fulfilled remedy. Initial counts: arrival_leak 1; explicit_loose_top 1; bare_arrival_agreement 0; replacement_offered 1; replacement_sent 0; retailer_leak 0; repurchase_intended 0.

Updated stage: Arrival leakage recurs across seven distinct visible TikTok accounts: P06, P08–P13. P06 and P13 independently describe loose/improperly screwed tops; P08 contextually confirms the problem and adds a free Sephora replacement sent. P09–P12 provide only terse agreement. Thus reported arrival leakage is independently repeated at the visible-account level within one reply branch, with four materially thinner observations. These are not seven verified independent humans or necessarily seven independently investigated events. Only two explicitly describe the closure problem; context cannot donate that detail, oxygen exposure or cleanup to all replies. Engagement for these seven is respectively 12, 5, 4, 4, 2, 0 and 0 displayed likes. P08 reports dispatch, not delivery or successful replacement use.

R01 separately reports Softwear–Void’s lid repeatedly unscrewing, including an in-pocket work leak, stained clothing, unrecoverable product and cost frustration. This adds retailer-role recurrence for the broader reported loose-closure/leakage problem across community comments and a retailer review, subject to unresolved cross-venue actor overlap. It does not corroborate arrival leakage, the unidentified TikTok SKU or a shared engineering cause. Its three-star review also explicitly recommends the product and intends repurchase because Void is a favorite. Complaint and loyalty coexist. Suggested click-lock/doe-foot changes are the reviewer’s proposals, not remedies implemented. Review helpfulness/likes and capture time are unavailable; verified-buyer and unrewarded metadata are not engagement or additional acquisition assertions.

Buying and loyalty consequences remain individually bounded. P17 reports an all-Experiment routine and Continuum in transit; P20 expresses broad buying intent, P32 tentative saving interest and P38 eagerness to try. None establishes packaging-caused checkout. P42 reports receipt and subsequent refillability discovery, which cannot establish that refillability motivated the acquisition. P04/P27 request bundles, not purchases. R01 alone explicitly intends repeat purchase; no completed repurchase, abandonment, return, delivered replacement or packaging-driven switch is established.

Reception is mixed across attributes: aesthetic/refill enthusiasm coexists with closure complaints and environmental/efficacy questions. Environmental benefits are unverified; the questions do not themselves disprove them. No supplied account directly denies arrival leakage, but this bounded selection cannot establish its prevalence. Manufacturing responsibility in R01 is the reviewer’s attribution, not verified root cause. All TikTok records share one brand-video venue, observed 2026-09-09T11:56:25.935Z; displayed dates lack a year. The capture contains 47 displayed bodies against 72 advertised comments, with only the specified branches expanded. Native comment IDs are unavailable. No context-only records were supplied. Counts below are updated focal source-account counts, not origin or event counts.
